# Intrinsic model selection oracle

`oracle.json` records fixed PilotDeck `cc7c4e653b15c8b2cec7bcf2d15d41d69396ae85` with Node 22, through `loadPilotConfig` on actual JSON configuration files. Ten primary-agent/memory/subagent/router selection locations are crossed with eleven Object.prototype property names, an ordinary model and a missing model, each with or without an own model definition (260 rows); inherited `__proto__` is separately exercised at all ten locations (10 rows); six additional own-definition shapes (null, false, true, array, string and number) are crossed with all ten positions (60 rows). Eight extra provider/prototype forms cross all ten positions (80 rows). Three intrinsic provider names cross all ten positions with inherited, own and earlier-invalid-provider cases (90 rows); three more rows distinguish field-specific whitespace behavior. Each row records the exact input, diagnostics and selected configuration sections or the error; the isolated PilotDeck home path alone is normalized to `<PILOT_HOME>`. A second isolated capture compared byte-identically.

The Rust test replays all 503 own, inherited, ordinary, missing, non-object-definition and provider/prototype rows against the recorded output. Inherited names are reference-truthiness behavior, never synthetic own model definitions. Inherited intrinsic provider lookups reproduce the observed TypeError at each selection site; raw model-catalog `__proto__` values are exercised against actual TS parsing; inherited `__proto__` has dedicated load rows and a separate runtime probe. `missing` rows exercise a true invalid reference rather than relaxing all unknown names.

To regenerate, set `PDRS_BASELINE` to the fixed baseline and use an isolated `HOME` and `PILOT_HOME`, then run `node record.mjs oracle.json`. Never use the user's real PilotDeck home.
